title: MCP Streamable HTTP door: ask the person in-client (elicitation) for a confirmation-gated action, via sessions for elicitation-capable clients
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5

Split from #33712 by maintainer ruling 6909391261 (Q1: in-client confirmation ships for the stdio door only; the HTTP door keeps the email/host approval path until this card). PR #34318 delivers in-client confirmation (step 1 of `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY`) on the long-lived stdio MCP server. The Streamable HTTP door stays on the #34202 hand-off. This card carries the HTTP half.

## Why the HTTP door cannot elicit today

Measured by the #33712 dev on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1 (report 6908665691):
- `handleHttpRequest` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` builds a fresh SDK `Server` for each POST (`enableJsonResponse: true`). The server that answers `tools/call` never saw `initialize`, so it holds no client capabilities.
- The client's answer to an `elicitation/create` comes back on a separate POST. A stateless door cannot route it to the pending request, because request ids are per instance.

## Candidate shape (not yet ruled; restating it is the restart's first step)

Sessions only for elicitation-capable clients:
- At `initialize`, the door issues `Mcp-Session-Id` and keeps a process-local record: capabilities, bound principal, expiry.
- Each POST seeds a per-request server from that record. A gated call answers as SSE only when it elicits.
- A response-only POST is routed to the in-flight request. DELETE ends the session.
- Every POST checks that its principal matches the session's bound principal; this needs pins.
- Non-capable clients stay byte-identical (plain JSON, hand-off).

A fully stateful door that binds tools at initialize was set aside on cost and on the frozen tool list it implies.

## Costs the shape must answer (isolated review of the #33712 options)

- Sticky routing: hosted routing must keep one `Mcp-Session-Id` on one process.
- SSE across the Worker hop: the hosted Worker-to-container hop must pass an SSE response through. `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (about :2757) says JSON was chosen to avoid exactly this.
- Long-held POSTs: a POST stays open while the person answers, up to the door's five-minute bound.
- Verb rules: the door answers only POST today, and GET/DELETE are 405 (#25759). Ending a session with DELETE reopens that rule.
- Written statelessness: ADR-0090 (about :487) and ADR-0101 (about :95-98) state that the HTTP door is stateless. A session design must amend them (governed text, maintainer review).
- Unverified: the MCP roadmap may be moving toward stateless operation without sticky sessions. Check that before building.

## Prerequisite

Hosted routing must be sticky on `Mcp-Session-Id`. Without it, the answer POST lands on another process and the question times out. The seat asked the repo:cloud seat on #6026.

Restart-when: a repo:cloud seat comment on #6026 confirms that hosted MCP HTTP routing is sticky on `Mcp-Session-Id` (or names the change that makes it so, which then becomes this card's `Blocked-by:`) · Restart-grade: p3

When restarted, also restore the no-service refusal's sentence "use a client that supports confirmation" (contract step 3). It was left out of #34202 and #34318 because it is false for every HTTP caller until this lands. (A door-aware message, true on stdio today, is a separate small card.)
